title: Choose Kedge's visual world
question: Dashboard first (judges watch it in a 2-minute video), landing page reuses the world. The roll assigned Transit Diagram. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.lineage: Harry Beck's 1933 London Underground diagram and the transit-map tradition
options.thesis: Every run is a line on a transit map: steps are stations, a drift is a spur that dead-ends, and Kedge's rollback is the line bending back to the last good station before it runs on to the green terminus.
options.viewport: Run list as a line index on the left (each run its own route colour); the selected run fills the field as one horizontal route: plan station, step stations with test counts, red drift spurs ending in a stop bar, a return curve to the checkpoint, and the green terminus labelled with the draft PR. Trace and Entire checkpoint as interchange rings.
options.risk: Reads as a novelty map if the line logic is loose; every bend must mean a real rollback.

raised.raise: State lives in fixed cells: filled mark holds, hollow did not, red strikes a drift, green confirms; never a free-floating badge.
Each run carries one sequence number as its headline (No. 07), the index is the only map.
Drift reads without colour: spurs carry a stop bar and hatch, so grayscale video and print still show the catch.
The same route renders at three scales (list thumbnail, run detail, PR card) from one drawing function.

options.label: VAR Review Room
options.thesis: The agent claims a goal; Kedge goes to the monitor: replay of the step, 'CHECK COMPLETE: goal disallowed, test deleted', then the corrected scoreline.
options.viewport: A replay timeline of the run with a 'CHECK' banner on each drift and a scoreline (tests passed) that flips when Kedge rules.
options.risk: Close to the near-black + neon look many dev dashboards ship; fun depends on judges knowing football.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: The batch is a departure board: each PR a flight, status reranks in place, a changed row holds its alert colour until noticed.
options.viewport: Batch board of 10 PRs ranked by status, the selected run as a boarding-pass detail.
options.case: Fuses well for the batch view; loses on clarity for a single run's rollback story.
options.risk: Familiar status-board look; the catch-and-rollback moment has no native shape.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.case: One type size and raked panels slow reading at video speed.
options.kept: Fixed state cells (filled holds, hollow not, red strikes, green confirms).

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.case: Coded labels hide the story judges must read instantly.
options.kept: One sequence number as the run's headline.

options.label: Exposure Record Sheets
options.case: Too indirect for the drift story.
options.kept: Conflict readable without colour (hatch + stop bar).

options.label: Emigre Bitmap Specimen
options.case: Specimen form has no place for run data.
options.kept: One form drawn at three scales.

options.label: Convention Circle Catalog
options.case: Thousands-of-cells density is wrong for 10 runs.
options.kept: Batch overview as whole cells, one per target.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean dev-tool dashboard: sidebar, run table, detail panel with a step timeline, status badges.
canonCard.viewport: Runs table on the left, run detail with a vertical step timeline on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other hackathon dashboard by design.
